title: bonsai.tasks/1
description: The tasks table, .bonsai/tasks.md (contract §7.5, spec §6): one row per task, newest id first, under a line naming the active task as contract §13's step 2 finds it (the one task reading running, or none and why). Built from the task files, format 0 and format 1 alike. Generated: written only by bonsai check --write, in the main checkout, and never by hand (the guard refuses an agent's edit, a tripwire); committed, never changed on a branch (rung 0 refuses one). Read by people (on GitHub and the Desk), agents and the studio. The task files and the log stay the truth: nothing reads a table to decide, and a table grants nothing. A stale table is a check warning everywhere, never a finding (contract §7.5). A markdown file whose frontmatter holds format and whose body holds the rest; a JSON Schema cannot describe a markdown table, so this schema describes what a reader returns (the frontmatter's fields, then what it reads from the body), and the body's lines and column order are formats/README.md's. A writer writes every field below, in this order, null, [] or {} where it does not apply (contract §2.2); a reader treats a missing field as null, keeps an unknown one and refuses a duplicate key.

format.description: The version line, the frontmatter's only key (contract §2.2); it carries a comment saying the file is generated and never edited by hand.

active.description: The line above the table: the active task when none is named (contract §13, step 2), its id or none and why.

id.description: The one task reading running, or null when there is none.

why.description: Why there is none, a few words; null when there is one.

tasks.description: One row per task file in the project's tasks folder that parses, newest id first (by its number); [] for none. A task file that does not parse under its format gives no row: check reports it as a finding (spec §6), and the active line then says none, naming it (contract §13: such a file makes the answer none).

status.description: The task's status as its file says: bonsai.task/1's closed list (its one home, task.schema.json), or a format-0 task's own word, shown as it is.

lane.description: The task's lane, or null for none.

started.description: The day work started, as the task file gives it; null before.

finished.description: The day the task reached done or cut, as the task file gives it; null before.
